target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and the extension typecheck are clean on the touched files.

target.title: feat(ui): dismissible sidebar attention chips
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar attention chips (failing/overdue cron jobs, expired/expiring model auth) cannot be dismissed. A known-and-accepted problem — e.g. a cron job the user will fix later — nags on every page of every session with no way to snooze it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a small ✕ button to each chip. Dismissals are deliberately client-side chrome (like nav width or dock layout), stored per gateway in localStorage under `openclaw.control.sidebarAttention.v1:<gateway-scope>` — dismissing a nag on one device should not acknowledge it everywhere, and no new gateway state/RPC surface is warranted for a snooze.

A dismissal is signature-keyed, not forever: each chip carries a signature of the sorted entity ids behind it (cron job ids, provider ids). The chip stays hidden only while the exact same set is affected:

- a new job fails / a new provider expires → signature changes → chip resurfaces
- the state clears (jobs recover, auth refreshed) → the stale dismissal is pruned, so a later recurrence surfaces again
- expiring → expired is a different chip kind, so an escalation always resurfaces as an error

Pruning runs only against loaded data, so an empty pre-load snapshot can't wipe valid snoozes.

Dismissals are multi-tab safe: writes merge with the persisted map (read-modify-write) instead of a tab-held snapshot, and tabs listen for `storage` events, so a dismissal in one tab hides the chip in every tab of that browser without losing the other tab's entries.

## User Impact

Each attention chip now has a subtle ✕ (visible on the right, `common.dismiss` tooltip). Clicking it hides that chip on this browser/device for as long as the underlying state is unchanged. The navigate-on-click behavior of the chip body is unchanged.

![attention chips with dismiss](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-attention-dismiss/attention-dismiss-dark.png)

## Evidence

- `ui/src/components/sidebar-attention.ts`: chips gain `kind` + `signature`; chip markup restructured to sibling navigate/dismiss buttons (buttons can't nest).
- `ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-dismissals.ts`: the per-gateway load/save/prune dismissal store lives in its own module (keeps the exports prod-imported for the deadcode ratchet and the snooze logic pure/unit-testable).
- `ui/src/styles/layout.css`: pill container split into `__open` + `__dismiss` buttons; dismiss is muted, brightens on hover.
- Tests: `pnpm test ui/src/components/sidebar-attention.test.ts` — 7 passed (signature construction incl. sorted ids and disabled-job exclusion; `pruneDismissals` keep/resurface/clear cases).
- Live-verified in the mock Control UI harness (dark mode): dismissing the "Model auth expired: Gemini" chip hides it and writes `{"modelAuthExpired":"google"}` to the gateway-scoped key; reload keeps it hidden while the state is unchanged; planting stale signatures (`google\nopenai`, `stale-provider`) resurfaces both chips and prunes the stored map back to empty.
- Multi-tab live-verified with two browser tabs on the mock harness: tab B saw tab A's dismissal without reload (storage event), tab B's own dismissal merged with A's (both entries persisted), and tab A synced back to zero chips.
- Reuses the existing `common.dismiss` i18n key — no locale changes needed.

target.title: improve(android): make gateway QR pairing prominent in Settings
target.body:
Closes #106186

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where pairing an Android phone with a gateway — the first-run action for every new device — was noisier and less discoverable than on iOS. Settings → Gateway had two identical "Add gateway" buttons in adjacent panels, buried setup-code entry inside a combined "Connection Setup" panel with always-expanded token/bootstrap/password fields, never showed discovered gateways (discovery already runs), and offered no nav-bar scan entry or first-run call to action.

Android follow-up to the iOS restructure (#106013 / #106111).

## Why This Change Was Made

`GatewaySettingsScreen` now mirrors the iOS ordering and entry points:

- **Nav-bar QR scan button** — `SettingsDetailFrame` gains an optional `trailingAction` slot; the Gateway screen puts a `QrCode2` scan button next to the title.
- **First-run hero** — a prominent "Scan QR to Pair" button shows while no gateway is paired (`gatewayShowsScanHero`).
- **Facts parity** — the metric panel adds Discovered / Default Agent / Agents / Instance ID rows (all data already on the ViewModel).
- **Diagnose** — copies the existing gateway diagnostics report (same helper chat uses).
- **Add Gateway panel** — one pairing panel owns Scan QR, setup-code paste + Connect, the "where do I get a code" help text, and a **discovered gateways list** with per-row Connect (`viewModel.connect(endpoint)`); discovery starts on screen entry like onboarding.
- **Manual Gateway panel** — host/port/TLS and credential fields move to the bottom as plumbing; its Save & Connect is now manual-only (setup code lives in Add Gateway).
- **Screenshot harness** — new `gateway` scene (`AndroidScreenshotScene.Gateway` → Settings tab + Gateway route) so this screen finally has deterministic capture; `scripts/android-screenshots.sh` captures it.

New strings ran the full native i18n pipeline (inventory, 21-locale translation, Android `strings.xml` + `NativeStringResources` projection). The discovered-row `host:port` subtitle is a format-only literal and is allowlisted in `android-app-i18n.ts` per existing convention (`$versionName-dev`, `> $line`).

## User Impact

Android users pairing a new gateway see Scan QR immediately — in the nav bar, as a hero while unpaired, and first in the Add Gateway panel — and can now tap nearby discovered gateways to connect directly. Manual/credential plumbing is out of the way but unchanged in behavior.

## Evidence

**Before → After** (emulator, deterministic screenshot fixture):

| Before (top) | After (top) | After (Add Gateway) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![before-top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-android-gateway-qr/before-gateway-top.png) | ![after-top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-android-gateway-qr/after-gateway-top.png) | ![after-mid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-android-gateway-qr/after-gateway-mid.png) |

Old layout for reference: [before-mid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-android-gateway-qr/before-gateway-mid.png) (duplicate Add gateway buttons, combined Connection Setup). Full bottom of new screen: [after-bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-android-gateway-qr/after-gateway-bottom.png).

- `:app:compilePlayDebugKotlin`, `:app:ktlintCheck`: green.
- Focused JVM tests green: `SettingsScreensTest` (new `gatewayShowsScanHero` / `gatewayDiscoveredRowSubtitle` cases + a source-order guard for the pairing-first layout), `AndroidScreenshotModeTest` (gateway scene mapping), `GatewayConfigResolverTest`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/android-app-i18n.test.ts`: pass.
- `native-app-i18n check`, `android-app-i18n check`, `apple-app-i18n check`: all pass.
- Gateway scene verified on emulator via `--es openclaw.screenshotScene gateway` (screenshots above); `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean on the touched script.

target.title: fix(chat): preserve explicit current-source sends in Control UI history
target.body:
Related: #104544
Related: #83494

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent could explicitly send a successful `message` tool reply to the exact current source conversation, while Control UI history omitted that delivered reply and showed only a later, different assistant final.

This PR addresses the explicit current-source `message` send slice of #104544. It does not address missing subagent lifecycle announcements, which are tracked separately in #105517.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit routes were excluded from message-tool history projection even when the resolved channel, account, target, and thread matched the current source conversation. The change adds a structured current-source route marker at the outbound owner and permits marker-backed successful explicit sends in the history projector.

Dry-run, suppressed, and explicit `ok: false` results remain excluded. Existing transcript delivery mirrors remain authoritative and are deduplicated.

## User Impact

Users who receive an explicit agent reply in the current Telegram/Slack source conversation can now see the same reply in Control UI session history. Later assistant output no longer replaces that delivered message in the dashboard.

Cross-channel, cross-account, cross-target, and cross-thread sends remain excluded from the current session history.

## Evidence

- Exact patch head: `20d3a5fa3ec980ae5946962a7caede3aabfc84fd`
- Exact replay base: `e0e0394d05c0f4d7d507b4dd753e96ce4be67510`
- Current exact-head Control UI proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29244520089 (running)
- Current exact-head fork patch CI: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29244520101 (running)
- Current upstream PR CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29244505142 (running)
- Previous exact-head Control UI proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29244196841 (passed at `c021024134c1f002433b3b881d8f19b0cef74a64`)
- Previous exact-head upstream PR CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29242075130 (passed at `5ca0701495e263fe78a784d270ca7d154ecdcfe4`)

The branch was replayed without patch-content changes onto upstream `main` at `e0e0394d05c0f4d7d507b4dd753e96ce4be67510`. A commit-by-commit range comparison matched all seven patch commits. The prior exact-head failures reproduced on the corresponding upstream baseline and were outside this PR's nine changed files: dangling msteams symbols, generated locale inventory drift, a plugin SDK baseline hash, and an asynchronous SQLite reliability helper mismatch. All of those upstream failures are repaired in this replay base.

Current upstream PR CI and the two fork workflows are now running against the repaired baseline. The upstream workflow tests the refreshed merge head, while both fork workflows pin the exact patch SHA.

## Risk And Rollback

Risk is limited to read-time history projection and the structured result metadata used to prove an exact current-source route. The marker is emitted only after trusted channel/account/target/thread resolution, and projection continues to reject existing non-success indicators.

Rollback is a straight revert of this PR. No config, schema, transcript migration, or persisted data rewrite is introduced.

## Documentation

No documentation change is needed. This restores consistency between an existing channel delivery path and the existing Control UI history surface without changing configuration or user-facing commands.
